question: Under MREC Rule 3.3(A), which of the following communications is included within the definition of a regulated "advertisement" for a Mississippi real estate licensee?
choice_a: A private, unsolicited text message between two personal friends discussing unrelated matters
choice_b: A verbal conversation between spouses about buying a home for their own use
choice_c: An internal company memo about administrative office procedures
choice_d: A public blog post, social media-networking website posting, or internet display promoting the licensee's real estate services
explanation: Rule 3.3(A) defines "advertisement" broadly to include oral, written, visual, printed, or electronic media, expressly listing e-mails, text messaging, public blogs, social media-networking websites, and internet displays as regulated advertising when used by or on behalf of a real estate licensee.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.3(A) (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-35.

question: Broker Daniels holds an individual broker's license issued in his own name, "Robert T. Daniels." He wants to begin advertising under the trade name "Magnolia Home Group" instead. Under MREC Rule 3.3(B), what must he do first?
choice_a: Obtain a license issued in that trade name (or the corresponding partnership/association/company/corporation license) before advertising under that name
choice_b: Nothing -- a broker may advertise under any name he chooses as long as his personal license number appears somewhere in the ad
choice_c: Notify MREC in writing within 30 days after he begins using the new name
choice_d: Register the trade name only with the Mississippi Secretary of State; MREC approval is not required
explanation: Rule 3.3(B) requires a broker to advertise in the name in which the license is issued (with only a descriptive occupational term allowed, e.g. "realty"); to advertise under a different trade name, partnership, association, company, or corporate name, the broker must first obtain a Commission-issued license in that name.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.3(B) (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-35.

question: Which of the following may a Mississippi broker add after her own licensed name in advertising without obtaining any additional license, per Rule 3.3(B)?
choice_b: A purely descriptive occupational term such as "Realty," "Real Estate," or "Property Management"
choice_c: The name of a national franchise the broker is not actually affiliated with
choice_d: A separate team or group name of the broker's own choosing
explanation: Rule 3.3(B) permits a broker to use a descriptive term after the broker's own licensed name to indicate the occupation engaged in -- the rule gives "realty," "real estate," and "property management" as examples. Anything beyond a descriptive occupational term (a franchise brand, invented trade name, etc.) requires the appropriate separate license.

question: An advertisement produced by a licensee affiliated with ABC Realty features the licensee's own name in large, bold 36-point type, while "ABC Realty" appears in small 10-point type tucked in a corner. Does this comply with MREC Rule 3.3(B)?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the brokerage's name appears anywhere in the ad, size does not matter
choice_b: Yes, because licensees are permitted to feature their personal brand more prominently than the firm
choice_c: No -- the Principal Broker's or Brokerage Firm's name must be identified using the same size or larger print than that used for a licensee, team member, or team in all advertising
choice_d: No, but only because the ad also needed the Multiple Listing Service logo
explanation: Rule 3.3(B) requires that the Principal Broker's or Brokerage Firm's name be prominently displayed, and specifically that the broker/firm be identified using the same size or larger print than that of a licensee, team member, or team in all advertising, in addition to including the broker's/firm's telephone number.

question: A team operating under Principal Broker Whitfield runs a paid Instagram ad campaign that prominently displays the team's own logo, the team members' names, and their personal cell numbers, but never mentions the sponsoring brokerage's name or phone number anywhere in the ad. Under MREC advertising rules, this social media ad is:
choice_a: Compliant, because Rule 3.3's requirements apply only to print and broadcast media, not internet or social media advertising
choice_b: Compliant, because teams are treated as independent brokerages for advertising purposes
choice_c: A violation only if the ad also fails to disclose the team members' individual license numbers
choice_d: A violation, because "advertisement" under Rule 3.3(A) expressly includes social media-networking websites and internet displays, and all such advertising must prominently display the Principal Broker's or Brokerage Firm's name and telephone number
explanation: Rule 3.3(A) explicitly includes social media-networking websites and internet displays within the definition of regulated "advertisement." Rule 3.3(B) then requires all advertising -- social media included -- to be under the direct supervision and in the name of the Principal Broker or Brokerage Firm, with that name and phone number prominently and conspicuously displayed. Omitting the brokerage's name and phone number from a social media ad violates this rule regardless of the medium used.

question: Before a Principal Broker or a licensee sponsored by that broker may advertise a property for sale or rent, or place a sign on the property, Rule 3.3(C) requires:
choice_a: Written authorization to do so from all owners of the property, or from an appointed person or entity with full authority to convey the property
choice_b: Verbal permission from the seller is sufficient if documented in the broker's file notes
choice_c: Only that the property first appear in the local Multiple Listing Service system
choice_d: Nothing further, if the property was previously advertised by another broker
explanation: Rule 3.3(C) states that no Principal Broker or licensee sponsored by that broker "shall in any way advertise property or place a sign on any such property offering the property for sale or rent without first obtaining the written authorization to do so by all owners of the property or by any appointed person or entity who also has full authority to convey the property."

question: Licensee Patterson is selling her own personal residence, which is not listed with any broker. She lists it on an internet marketplace and places a "For Sale by Owner" yard sign. Under Rule 3.3(D), what is she required to do?
choice_a: Nothing, because she is selling her own property as a private individual, not acting as an agent for a client
choice_b: Disclose that she is a licensed real estate agent in every form of advertising used, including the yard sign itself
choice_c: Disclose her license status only in the eventual sales contract, not in advertising
choice_d: Disclose her license status only if she is currently on active license status; inactive licensees are exempt
explanation: Rule 3.3(D) requires that when a licensee advertises their own property for sale, purchase, or exchange (property not listed with a broker), the licensee must indicate that they are licensed, and this disclosure "must be made in all forms of advertising enumerated in Rule 3.3(A), including the 'for sale' sign." The rule further requires disclosure of licensed status whether the licensee is on active or inactive status.

question: Which of the following advertising practices is expressly prohibited as an unlawful "blind advertisement" under MREC Rule 3.3(D)?
choice_a: A yard sign that includes the brokerage's logo along with the listing agent's name
choice_b: A digital ad that lists the property address along with the brokerage's name and license number
choice_c: A newspaper classified ad for a listed property that gives only a phone number and a P.O. box, with no indication that the advertiser is a real estate licensee
choice_d: A radio ad that names both the Principal Broker and the brokerage firm
explanation: Rule 3.3(D) prohibits a licensee from advertising to sell, buy, exchange, auction, rent, or lease property in a manner suggesting the offer is being made by a private party not engaged in the real estate business, and specifically states that "no advertisement shall be inserted by a licensee in any publication where only a post office box number, telephone number, e-mail address or street address appears" -- every licensee's ad must indicate that the advertiser is licensed in real estate.

question: Under MREC Rule 3.5(A), all of the following are required elements for a group of licensees to qualify as an approved "Real Estate Team or Group" EXCEPT:
choice_a: Each member works under the direct supervision of the same Principal Broker
choice_b: Members represent themselves to the public as being part of a Team or Group under a specific team/group name
choice_c: All real estate activity is conducted from the primary or branch office where the members' individual licenses are displayed
choice_d: Each team member must independently hold an active broker's license (salespersons may not participate)
explanation: Rule 3.5(A) requires active real estate licensees (not necessarily brokers) who work together under the same Principal Broker, represent themselves publicly as a team/group under a specific name, and conduct all activity from the office where their licenses are displayed. There is no requirement that every team member individually hold a broker's license -- active salespersons may be team members.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.5(A) (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-3(4); §73-35-18(3); §73-35-21(d).

question: Rule 3.5(C) requires every real estate Team to appoint a Team Leader who must meet which qualification?
choice_a: The Team Leader must be a Broker Associate with a minimum of one year of real estate experience, holding supervisory responsibility over team members under the Principal Broker
choice_b: The Team Leader must be the Principal Broker of the firm personally
choice_c: The Team Leader must be a state-approved continuing education instructor
choice_d: There is no minimum experience requirement; any active licensee on the team may serve as Team Leader
explanation: Rule 3.5(C) requires that all teams appoint a Team Leader who is a Broker Associate with a minimum of one year's real estate experience, with supervisory responsibility (under the Principal Broker) over team members; the Team Leader may face disciplinary action for violations committed by team members under their supervision.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.5(C) (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-3(4); §73-35-18(3); §73-35-21(d).

question: When a properly approved Team Name is used in advertising under Rule 3.5(D), how must the Team's name be sized relative to the Brokerage Firm's name?
choice_a: The Team name must always be larger than the Brokerage Firm's name to help build the team's independent brand
choice_b: The Team name must be identified with the same size or smaller print than that of the Brokerage, and situated near the Brokerage Firm's name
choice_c: There is no size requirement for team names, only for individual licensee names
choice_d: The Team name may be any size as long as it appears on a separate page of the advertisement
explanation: Rule 3.5(D) requires that the name of the Team be situated near the name of the Brokerage Firm and identified with the same sized or smaller print than that of the Brokerage -- the mirror image of the requirement under Rule 3.3(B) that the broker/firm name be the same size or larger than an individual licensee's name, both serving the same goal of keeping the sponsoring Brokerage Firm clearly identifiable.

question: A group of five licensees under Principal Broker Ortiz wants to register and advertise under the team name "Coastal Realty Group." Under MREC Rule 3.5(E), is this name permissible?
choice_a: Yes, any name chosen by the team leader and approved internally is permissible
choice_b: Yes, as long as the word "Team" also appears somewhere in the name
choice_c: No -- team names may not include terms such as "real estate brokerage," "realty," "real estate," or "company," because such terms could suggest the team is an independent brokerage
choice_d: No, because team names must always include the Principal Broker's personal surname
explanation: Rule 3.5(E) states that neither team names nor team advertising should suggest that the team is an independent real estate brokerage, and specifically prohibits team names from including terms such as "real estate brokerage," "realty," "real estate," or "company." "Coastal Realty Group" contains the prohibited term "Realty" and would not be permitted.

question: Mississippi Broker Reyes enters into a cooperative agreement with an out-of-state broker (not Mississippi-licensed) to co-market a Mississippi listing, and the nonresident broker wants to place a yard sign on the property. Under Rule 3.1(C), what must occur?
choice_a: The nonresident broker may place the sign freely once a cooperative agreement has been filed with the Commission
choice_b: Only the nonresident broker's sign may be displayed, since it represents the buyer's side of the transaction
choice_c: Signage rules under Rule 3.1 apply only to auctions, not standard residential listings
choice_d: The nonresident broker cannot place any sign on the Mississippi property without the written consent of the cooperating Mississippi broker, and once consent is given, the Mississippi broker's sign must be placed prominently and in close proximity to the nonresident broker's sign
explanation: Rule 3.1(C) requires written consent from the cooperating Mississippi broker before a nonresident broker may place a sign on Mississippi property, and once consent is obtained, the Mississippi broker's sign must be placed in a prominent location in close proximity to the nonresident broker's sign. A Mississippi broker who fails to have their name listed in such advertising or fails to cross-list the property in writing is deemed in violation of Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-11 and is subject to license revocation or suspension.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.1(C) (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-11, §73-35-35.

question: An out-of-state land developer wants to advertise an out-of-state property directly to Mississippi consumers (not through a national publication). Under MREC Rule 7.1, what must the developer do first?
choice_a: First contact the Mississippi Real Estate Commission to have the property approved for advertising; MREC may, at the developer's cost, conduct an on-site inspection
choice_b: Nothing -- out-of-state property is outside MREC's jurisdiction
choice_c: Register the property only with the Mississippi Secretary of State
choice_d: Obtain approval only from the local Multiple Listing Service covering the target Mississippi market
explanation: Rule 7.1 requires out-of-state land developers who wish to advertise out-of-state property in Mississippi (except in national publications) to first contact MREC to have the property approved for advertising. MREC may in its discretion conduct an on-site inspection at the developer's cost, and any Mississippi broker acting as the developer's agent or representative is responsible for the truth and accuracy of the representations, offerings, and advertising of such properties in Mississippi.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 7.1 (Rev. 02/21/2025); Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-35.

question: Beyond the Commission's administrative advertising rules, Mississippi's licensing statute itself, Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21, provides an independent statutory ground for suspension or revocation of a license based on:
choice_a: Only advertising errors that actually result in a completed sale
choice_b: Any misleading or untruthful advertising, as well as a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or false promises made through any medium of advertising
choice_c: Advertising violations only when reported by a competing broker
choice_d: Advertising practices that violate federal, but not Mississippi, truth-in-advertising standards
explanation: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1) lists "any misleading or untruthful advertising" as an independent statutory ground for license suspension or revocation, alongside "pursuing a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation or making false promises through agents or salespersons or any medium of advertising or otherwise." This statutory basis for discipline operates independently of, and in addition to, MREC's administrative advertising rules found in Rule 3.3.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. §73-35-21(1)(c)-(d) (1972, as amended); MREC Rules and Regulations, Rule 3.3 (Rev. 02/21/2025).
